## Problem

A `solve --tool codex` run against [formal-ai#902](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/902) did all of its work — it opened [formal-ai#913](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/913), got every CI check green, and Codex closed its turn normally — and was then declared **failed**:

```
❌ Codex exited 0 but the run did not complete — treating as failure
   • Codex session ended without completing its turn (turn.started=2, turn.completed=1, turn.failed=0)
```

A ["🚨 Solution Draft Failed"](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/913#issuecomment-5166232530) comment was posted on a pull request that was complete — and was merged four hours later with all checks passing.

Codex emitted exactly **one** `turn.started`. The second one came from its own OTEL trace on **stderr**: `codex_otel.log_only: event.name="codex.tool_result" … output=` records dump the raw stdout of every command Codex runs, and the task under test was driving another agent CLI, so that agent's NDJSON was replayed verbatim (run log lines 9322–9331). `executeCodexCommand` fed stderr through the same parser as the `--json` stdout protocol, so a line printed *about* the run was counted *as* the run. The dump was truncated (`Warning: truncated output`) before the nested `turn.completed`, which is why the counts went out of balance.

The contamination is visible in the run's own summary — Codex has no `config`, `log`, `tool_use` or `formal_ai_completion` events:

```
📊 Codex JSON events: thread.started=2, turn.started=2, … config=1, log=12, tool_use=2, message=1, formal_ai_completion=1, unknown=40, turn.completed=1
```

## Fix

Three layers, deliberately redundant:

- **A — stream separation.** `parseCodexExecJsonOutput(output, state, model, { source })` treats only stdout as protocol. Protocol-shaped JSON on stderr goes to a new `telemetryEventCounts` bucket and never touches `eventCounts`, `sessionId`, `tokenUsage` or the error buckets. The *text* diagnostics that legitimately live on stderr (token/model diagnostics, the #2102 plugin-install rejection) still run there unchanged.
- **B — order-aware completion gate.** `getCodexCompletionHealth` now uses the ordered `turnLifecycle`: incomplete ⇔ the last lifecycle event is a `turn.started`. A stray extra `turn.started` can no longer fail a completed run; the genuine #1990 shape (stream ends mid-turn) still fails. Falls back to the old count comparison when no lifecycle is present.
- **C — diagnostics** (the issue's "add debug output so the next iteration can find the root cause" requirement): `🪞 Echoed protocol-shaped lines on codex stderr (ignored, not codex events): …` and `🔁 Codex turn lifecycle: turn.started → turn.completed`.

## Codebase-wide sweep

The issue asks for the fix to be applied everywhere the defect exists. All six tool integrations were audited:

| Tool | Parsed stderr as protocol? | Consequence | Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| codex | yes | this incident; session-id hijack; inflated usage; false errors | **fixed** |
| qwen | yes | an echoed `{"type":"error"}` lands in `state.errors`, and qwen fails a run outright when `errors.length > 0`; both streams also shared one line buffer | **fixed** (source separation + independent buffers) |
| opencode | yes, deliberately (#1263) | usage/summary skew only — no terminal-event gate | behaviour unchanged, stderr records now **counted and reported** |
| gemini | no (stderr used as text) | — | none |
| claude | no (stdout-only stream-json) | — | none |

## Reproduction and tests

- `tests/test-issue-2136-codex-telemetry-echoed-turn-events.mjs` — 21 assertions across parser separation, the order-aware gate, verbose diagnostics, an end-to-end `executeCodexCommand` run whose stderr replays the incident block, and the qwen parity cases. Verified to fail before the fix (5 passed / 11 failed) and pass after.
- `experiments/issue-2136/reproduce-parser-confusion.mjs` reproduces the exact failure message offline from the incident's stdout/stderr split:

```
stderr parsed as protocol (old): turn.started=2 turn.completed=1 → healthy=false  ← the false failure
   reason: Codex session ended without completing its turn (turn.started=2, turn.completed=1, turn.failed=0); …
stderr treated as telemetry (new): turn.started=1 turn.completed=1 → healthy=true
```

## Case study and upstream report

- `docs/case-studies/issue-2136/` — full timeline with log line numbers, the requirement-by-requirement table, root causes RC1–RC4, rejected alternatives, prior art, and `raw/` with the complete 26,824-line run log (gzipped), the issue JSON, the failure-comment JSON and the target-PR JSON.
- Reported upstream: **[openai/codex#36804](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/36804)** — `codex exec --json` splices raw, unescaped, multi-line tool stdout into stderr OTEL traces, with reproduction, impact, the workaround, and three concrete fix suggestions.

Fixes #2136

Issue: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2136

Codex's stderr carries OTEL tracing text whose `codex.tool_result` records
dump the raw stdout of every command codex runs. When the task drives another
agent CLI, that dump replays NDJSON that is byte-identical to codex's own
protocol, so the echoed `turn.started` was counted as codex's own and the
#1990 completion gate failed a run that had actually completed.

- parseCodexExecJsonOutput takes a `source`; only stdout is protocol, stderr
  JSON goes to telemetryEventCounts (diagnostics only)
- getCodexCompletionHealth uses the ordered turnLifecycle: incomplete means the
  last lifecycle event is a turn.started
- same stream separation for qwen (its stderr echo could raise a false error)
  and visibility for opencode stderr JSON records
- verbose diagnostics for echoed lines and the turn lifecycle
- reproducing test built from the captured incident log

Refs #2136
